name: Cinnamon extract
summary: Insulin sensitivity support; safety screen: liver disease; anticoagulant medication caution; pregnancy high-dose caution.
description: Cinnamon extract supports glucose metabolism, plausibly via insulin sensitivity and carbohydrate handling; evidence is mixed but mechanistic signals are relevant.
safetyNotes: Cassia cinnamon can contain coumarin; avoid aggressive high-dose chronic use with liver concerns.

sources.title: The effect of cinnamon supplementation on glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: An updated systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
sources.citation: PubMed PMID 37818728. Minimal citation row added from existing workbook PMID; title/year/journal still require PubMed metadata extraction.
sources.note: evidence citation lookup; PMID source present in Evidence_Register

contraindications: Existing liver disease or elevated liver enzymes due to cassia-type cinnamon's coumarin content which can exceed established safety intake limits with regular use and has been linked to liver-enzyme elevation or liver injury case reports
concurrent diabetes medication or insulin due to additive blood-sugar-lowering effect and hypoglycemia risk
concurrent acetaminophen or other liver-metabolized medication due to combined hepatic burden
true Ceylon cinnamon contains only trace coumarin and carries a substantially lower version of this risk.
evidence_grade_explanation: The recorded grade (moderate evidence) and evidence tier (preliminary evidence) conflict, so the weaker signal is published pending review.
evidence_rationale: Strongest recorded design is a meta-analysis, drawn from 2 recorded studies, 2 in people.
